newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS RALLY FROM TWO-GOAL DEFICIT TO EDGE FLYERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS RALLY FROM TWO-GOAL DEFICIT TO EDGE FLYERS.

text.p: The Rangers erased a two-goal deficit and Mike Richter stopped all 19 shots he faced over the final two periods as New York rallied for a 3-2 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers Monday.

The Rangers were without captain Mark Messier, who has a thigh injury but may return for a rematch between the two teams Thursday. New York killed all seven of the Flyer power plays and went 2-for-7 with the man advantage.
Alexander Karpovtsev and Brian Leetch scored 51 seconds apart late in the second period with Eric Lindros in the penalty box serving a double-minor for high-sticking.
Lindros was sent to the box for cracking his stick over the back of Rangers enforcer Shane Churla.
"It's a physical game and during the course of the game sticks are going to get up," Lindros said.
"I'm sure he is used to people goading him," Churla said. "He didn't make the right decision on how to use his stick. He should have been gone right there.
"If there is any justice he shouldn't be there (on Thursday). Eric Lindros is Eric Lindros, a great player, just who he is doesn't give him a credit card to use his stick however he wants."
All three New York goals were scored by defencemen as Doug Lidster got the Rangers on the board midway through the second period after Philadelphia took a 2-0 lead.
The win moved the Rangers two points ahead of Pittsburgh for the fifth playoff spot and within a point of Florida for fourth and home-ice advantage in the first round.

Pat Falloon and Lindros scored three minutes apart in the first period for the Flyers, who failed to regain first place in the Eastern Conference from New Jersey, remaining one point behind. The Flyers host the Devils in both teams' season finale Sunday.
"This game hurts," said Flyers coach Terry Murray. "It's a big loss for us as far as first place overall. We had an opportunity to get a point back but we didn't show the composure or discipline."
"We were up 2-0 with 10 minutes to go and take two penalties and don't kill them," Flyers winger Rod Brind'Amour said.
Richter stopped 13 shots in the final period, including a pair of point-blank stops on Dale Hawerchuk early in the period and another on John LeClair with just over three minutes to play.

In Montreal, Benoit Brunet scored the tie-breaking goal with 3:10 left in the third period and Jocelyn Thibault made 25 saves as the Canadiens improved their playoff chances with a 2-1 victory over the New York Islanders.

With the score tied 1-1, Brunet attempted to redirect Vladimir Malakhov's point shot in the slot but the puck stopped. Brunet wheeled around and threw a backhander at the net and it hit defenceman Scott Lachance before fluttering over goaltender Tommy Salo's arm.

Malakhov tallied in the first period for Montreal, which has won four of its last six games. The win gave the Canadiens 74 points and kept them one point ahead of eighth-place Hartford in the Eastern Conference.

Todd Bertuzzi scored for the Islanders, who are 0-3-1 following a season-high five-game unbeaten streak. New York is five points behind Hartford with three games to play, including Wednesday's home contest against Montreal.

In Hartford, Geoff Sanderson scored twice in a 3:53 span of the third period and the Whalers tallied four unanswered goals to solidify their playoff standing with a 4-2 victory over the Buffalo Sabres.
Sanderson has seven goals in six games against the Sabres this season.
Keith Primeau and Steve Chiasson also scored for Hartford, which is 4-1-1 in its last six games following a six-game losing streak.
In Phoenix, Dallas Drake and Joe Nieuwendyk exchanged second-period goals as the Dallas Stars and Coyotes skated to a 2-2 tie.

Jeremy Roenick also scored and Nikolai Khabibulin made 28 saves for the Coyotes, who are 6-3-2 in their last 11 games. The tie moved Phoenix into a fourth-place tie with Anaheim in the West, one point ahead of sixth-place Edmonton.
Jere Lehtinen tallied for Dallas, which has already clinched the Central Division. The Stars, 9-1-4 in their last 14 games, moved within three points of top-seeded Colorado.

In San Jose, Markus Naslund and Sergei Nemchinov had third-period tallies and Kirk McLean stopped 24 shots as the Vancouver Canucks kept their slim playoff hopes alive with a 3-2 victory over the Sharks.
Vancouver moved within four points of the eighth and final playoff spot in the West but has just two games remaining.
Tony Granato and Ville Peltonen had goals for the Sharks, who played the final period without star winger Owen Nolan, who strained his groin.
